subject: environmental-science
title: Water in the Environment: Saving Water
welcome_lead: Small drips add up — saving water saves money and energy.
meta_desc: KS3 environmental science: water saving, virtual water.
final_note: Even the food we eat has a water cost.

concepts.def: Water used to make a product.
Lightly used water reused for plants.
Tap part mixing air to save water.
Lost water from a pipe or tap.
Total water you use, direct and hidden.
Container collecting rain from a roof.

walkthroughs.body_html: A burger needs about 2400 litres of water to grow the wheat, beef and salad. That's virtual water.
Short showers, full washing loads, fixing leaks and using tap aerators cut huge amounts of water.
A rain barrel catches roof rain. Greywater from a bath can water plants. Mulch saves moisture in soil.

mcqs.q: How does the Brundtland Report define sustainable development?
options: Stopping all development immediately.
Environmental protection at all costs.
About 50 percent.
Meeting present needs without compromising future generations' ability to meet theirs.

mcqs.q: Why is burning fossil fuels considered to disrupt the carbon cycle?
options: It creates new carbon that did not exist before.
About 50 percent.
It releases carbon stored for millions of years much faster than the cycle can absorb.
It removes carbon permanently.

mcqs.q: Roughly what proportion of energy passes from one trophic level to the next?
